svg.aria-label: Bridge explaining why the Cash Book bank balance differs from the Bank Statement balance: Cash Book omissions vs Timing Differences
svg.text: Why Cash Book Balance ≠ Bank Statement Balance (The Two Causes)
Remember the Mirror Rule: A DEPOSIT is a DEBIT in your Cash Book, but a CREDIT on the Bank Statement!
Cause 1: Items on Bank Stmt NOT Yet in Cash Book
FIX: Update the ADJUSTED CASH BOOK!
Put on DEBIT side of Adjusted Cash Book (+ Cash):
• Credit Transfers / Direct Deposits from customers
• Dividends & Bank Interest Received directly
• Cash Book error where a receipt was understated
Put on CREDIT side of Adjusted Cash Book (− Cash):
• Bank Charges & Overdraft Interest
• Standing Orders (fixed auto-pay e.g. rent/loan)
• Direct Debits (variable auto-pay e.g. electricity)
• Dishonored (NSF / Bounced) Customer Cheques
Cause 2: Timing Differences (In Cash Book, Not Bank)
FIX: Put ONLY on the BANK RECONCILIATION STMT!
1. Unpresented Cheques (Outstanding Cheques)
Cheques WE wrote & credited in Cash Book, but the
supplier has NOT cashed them at the bank yet.
→ ADD to Adjusted Cash Book Balance!
2. Late Lodgements (Deposits in Transit)
Cash/cheques WE deposited & debited in Cash Book,
still clearing — NOT yet credited by the bank!
→ SUBTRACT from Adjusted Cash Book Balance!
The Bank Statement Mirror Rule (Never Get Confused by Dr/Cr on a Bank Statement!)
Positive Bank Balance: Cash Book = DEBIT | Bank Statement = CREDIT · Bank Overdraft: Cash Book = CREDIT | Bank Statement = DEBIT!
